about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2014 only.

rows.name: Table of contents
rows.what_it_is: The report's index, grouped under section banners (ADMINISTRATION, ACCOUNTANT, TREASURER/TAX COLLECTOR, TOWN SERVICES, PROTECTION OF PERSONS & PROPERTY, PLANNING, EDUCATION, TOWN CLERK, MISCELLANEOUS INFORMATION), with the page each item starts on.
rows.layout: two-column list under section banner headings, spread over two pages
rows.notes: NOTABLE: four entries are listed as 'no report' rather than omitted - 'Agricultural Commission - no report', 'Conservation Commission - no report', 'Cultural Council - no report', 'Veterans Agent- no report'. That is an explicit record of what is MISSING from the year, which FY2013 does not provide. The last entry is 'Town Office/Department Hours/Phone Numbers Back Cover'.

rows.name: Lunenburg town profile facts
rows.what_it_is: A short fact sheet: year incorporated, registered voters, tax rate, form of government, town meeting and election dates, land area and road mileage.
rows.layout: eight label-dash-value lines
rows.notes: Values: Year Incorporated 1728; Registered Voters 7059; FY'14 Tax Rate $17.99; Open Town Meeting Government - Five Member Board of Selectmen; Annual Town Meeting 1st Saturday in May; Annual Town Election 3rd Saturday in May; Area 26.63 Square Miles; Road Miles about 100. NOTE the narrative on the very next page says '26.4 square miles' - the two pages disagree. The DPW section on page 52 says '86 miles of paved streets' against 'about 100' road miles here. FY2013's report has no equivalent page at all.

rows.name: State and federal elected officials with contact details
rows.what_it_is: Governor, Attorney General, both US Senators, the US Representative, the state Senator and the two state Representatives, each with office address and phone.
rows.layout: two columns of address blocks under banner headings
rows.notes: Records which precincts each state rep covers: 'House of Representatives - 37th Middlesex District (Lunenburg Precincts A, C, D)' Jennifer E. Benson; 'House of Representatives- 3rd Worcester District (Lunenburg Precinct B)' Stephen L. DiNatale. That precinct split explains why State Election Question 5 on page 163 has votes in Precinct B only.

rows.name: Elected town officials with term expiry
rows.what_it_is: Every elected town board and office, with each member's name and the year their term expires.
rows.columns: board / office (with term length) | name | term expiry year
rows.layout: board heading, then one 'Name - Year' line per member
rows.notes: Format is 'Board of Assessors - 3 year term' then 'Christopher M. Comeau - 2015'. Boards listed: Assessors, Health, Selectmen, Cemetery Commission, Constable, Housing Authority (5 year term), Library Trustees, Moderator, Park Commission, Planning Board, School Committee, Sewer Commission, Town Clerk, Trust Fund Commission. FY2014 has a PARK COMMISSION that does not appear as an elected board in FY2013's roster.

rows.name: Appointed officials, committees and boards
rows.printed_heading: APPOINTED OFFICIALS / TERMS ARE FOR ONE YEAR UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED.
rows.what_it_is: Every appointed position, committee and commission, with the appointee's name and, where the term is longer than a year, the expiry year.
rows.columns: committee / position | term expiry year | name | represented body
rows.layout: two columns of committee blocks; committee name in caps, then indented 'YYYY  Name' lines, or 'Name, Body Representative' lines for representative seats
rows.notes: Vacancies are recorded explicitly (' Vacancy', 'ASSISTANT BUILDING INSPECTOR / Vacancy'). Representative seats spell out which body the person represents ('Toby Bakaysa, Planning Board Representative'). Term lengths are marked on the heading ('BOARD OF APPEALS-5 years', 'CONSERVATION COMMISSION - 3 years'). The standing caveat 'TERMS ARE FOR ONE YEAR UNLESS OTHERWISE INDICATED.' is reprinted at the top of every one of the five pages.

rows.name: Combined balance sheet, all fund types and account groups
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG, MASSACHUSETTS / COMBINED BALANCE SHEET / ALL FUND TYPES AND ACCOUNT GROUPS / FOR THE YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2014
rows.what_it_is: The town's balance sheet at 30 June 2014: assets, liabilities and fund equity, in six parallel fund columns.
rows.columns: line item | GENERAL FUND | SPECIAL REVENUE FUND | ENTERPRISE FUNDS | CAPITAL PROJECT FUND | FIDUCIARY FUND TYPES TRUST and AGENCY | ACCT. GROUP GENERAL LONG-TERM DEBT
rows.layout: line items down the left, six money columns; amounts appear on the same line as their label
rows.printed_total: TOTAL ASSETS $6,152,141.84 / $1,290,055.14 / $7,709,003.18 / $317,222.98 / $2,300,308.92 / $22,140,230; TOTAL LIABILITIES/FUND EQUITY ties to the same figures
rows.notes: Because empty cells collapse, a line with only two figures does not say which columns they belong to - column assignment needs the x-positions. Otherwise this is directly readable, unlike FY2013's version of the same table. Line items include an unusual FY-by-FY breakout of uncollected real estate taxes back to FY07, and DUE TO WATER DISTRICT $32,571.63, WARRANTY DEPOSITS $3,622.50, MEADOW WOODS WATER BETTERMENT REC $1,127,070.97. Note an ENTERPRISE FUNDS column exists here that FY2013's balance sheet does not break out.

rows.name: General fund revenues pie chart
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of FY2014 general fund revenue by source with percentage labels.
rows.layout: pie chart; only the slice labels are in the text layer
rows.notes: PROPERTY TAXES 65.18%, MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE 4.64%, STATE-LOCAL AID 23.62%, ALL OTHER 6.56%. Unlike FY2013's chart, the property tax slice label survives, so this year's chart is complete.

rows.name: Receipts by revenue account, FY2014
rows.what_it_is: Every general fund revenue account collected in FY2014 with its amount, grouped under TAXES & EXCISES, INTEREST, DEMANDS, FEES, DEPARTMENTAL REVENUE, LICENSES/PERMITS, STATE REVENUE, FINES & FORFEITS, FEDERAL REVENUE, EARNINGS ON INVESTMENTS and TRANSFERS FROM OTHER FUNDS, with a summary box.
rows.layout: three label/amount column pairs across one page, plus a SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS box in the third column
rows.printed_total: SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS: TAXES & EXCISES $21,630,885.64; FEES $556,792.92; LICENSES AND PERMITS $293,937.65; STATE REVENUE $7,273,215.19; SPECIAL ASSESSMENTS $55,152.53; FINES & FORFEITS $48,537.50; INVESTMENT INCOME $14,811.95; TRANSFER FROM OTHER FUNDS $807,442.00; NON RECURRING REVENUE $108,604.09; GRAND TOTAL $30,789,379.47
rows.notes: THE FY2013 VERSION OF THIS TABLE HAD ITS THIRD COLUMN OF AMOUNTS CLIPPED OFF THE PAGE. Here all three columns are complete, including the entire summary box and the GRAND TOTAL - so FY2014 gives you the summary that FY2013 does not. Extraction caveat: because it is three column-pairs on one line, a naive line parse will merge three different accounts. Anchors: REAL ESTATE TAXES $19,317,359.78; CH 70 SCHOOL AID $5,516,107.00; MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE $1,427,170.04; SEC 2D CH 29 LOTTERY, BEANO $915,592.00; MSBA REIMB-SCHOOL $499,098.00; BUILDING PERMITS $174,757.15 (up from $61,956.45 in FY2013); SCHOOL BASED MEDICARE REIMB $105,052.59; ZONING INCENTIVE PAYMENT $99,000.00 (new line, absent in FY2013); PEDDLER'S LICENSE $80.00; TOWN PROPERTY HAYING $750.00; BOARDING OF DOGS $25.00.

rows.name: General fund expenditures pie chart
rows.what_it_is: Pie chart of FY2014 general fund spending by function with percentage labels.
rows.layout: pie chart; slice labels only
rows.notes: Education 54.33%, All Other 12.40%, Debt Service 9.19%, General Govt Unclassified 7.71%, Public Safety 7.86%, Department of Public Works 4.60%, General Government 3.89%. The Education slice label survives here; in FY2013's chart it did not. Comparable across years except that FY2013's chart has no 'Education' label at all.

rows.name: General fund appropriations and expenditures, line by line
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / GENERAL FUND APPROPRIATIONS / SUMMARY & CLASSIFICATION OF ACCOUNTS / FISCAL YEAR 2014
rows.what_it_is: The town accountant's detail of every general fund budget line: appropriated, funds forwarded from FY2013, total available, total expended, total encumbered, and balance returned to revenue. Grouped by function (GENERAL GOVERNMENT, PUBLIC SAFETY, HEALTH AND SANITATION, DPW, PUBLIC ASSISTANCE, SCHOOLS, LIBRARY, CULTURE & RECREATION, UNCLASSIFIED, DEBT AND INTEREST, STATE & COUNTY ASSESSMENTS, TRANSFERS TO OTHER FUNDS), with a departmental subtotal line after each department.
rows.grain: one budget line (payroll / other expenses within a department), with a subtotal row per department
rows.columns: PROGRAM NAME | APPROPRIATED | FUNDS FORWARD | TOTAL AVAILABLE | TOTAL EXPENDED | TOTAL ENCUMBERED | BALANCE TO REVENUE
rows.layout: program name at left, up to six money columns; department subtotal appears on its own unlabelled line directly below the department's detail lines
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTAL $31,356,354.04 appropriated / $31,356,354.04 available / $30,955,803.56 expended / $233,181.84 encumbered / $167,368.64 balance to revenue. Footer: 'fwd - forward from FY 2013 $211,530.04' - which ties exactly to the FY2013 report's carried-forward figure.
rows.notes: Directly extractable except for column assignment: subtotal lines carry no label, and lines with blank cells collapse. Carry-forward amounts are printed on their own line ABOVE the department they belong to and marked 'fwd' or 'srt' ('$18,724.78 fwd' above Technology Director; '$4,689.00 srt' above Town Manager) - do not read them as ordinary amounts. Key anchors: School Department payroll $11,045,156.17 / other expenses $5,077,965.83 / total $16,123,122.00 appropriated, $16,081,466.40 expended; Monty Tech Assessment $757,805.00 appropriated / $708,561.00 expended; Health Insurance CH 32B $1,682,916.56 available / $1,672,215.22 expended; Principal Serial Loans $2,054,987.00; Interest Serial Loans $780,664.00; County Retirement Assessment $725,771.00; Choice Tuitions $475,249.00 appropriated / $423,947.00 expended; Charter Tuitions $548,449.00 / $509,381.00; Transfer to Stabilization Fund $286,958.00; Transfer to Capital Project Fund $631,687.00. Two assessments came in OVER budget with negative balances: Mosquito Control ($1,894.00) and Special Education ($9,862.00) against a $0.00 appropriation.

rows.name: Special revenue funds: grants, gifts, revolving and enterprise accounts
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR ENDING 6/30/14
rows.what_it_is: Every special revenue fund with its opening balance, receipts, disbursements and closing balance, grouped by GENERAL GOVERNMENT, SCHOOL DEPARTMENT, PUBLIC SAFETY, PARKS & RECREATION, COUNCIL ON AGING, LIBRARY, CEMETERIES and UNCLASSIFIED.
rows.columns: PROGRAM NAME | FORWARD 7/1/2013 | TOTAL RECEIPTS | TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS | BALANCE FWD 7/1/2014
rows.layout: fund name at left, four money columns; dormant funds print only two identical figures (open and close)
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTAL $2,209,000.67 forward / $5,443,849.18 receipts / $5,052,956.22 disbursements / $2,599,893.63 balance forward. The opening $2,209,000.67 ties exactly to the FY2013 report's special revenue grand total.
rows.notes: Fully readable, but a dormant fund prints only its opening and closing figures with the two middle columns absent, so a naive parse will mis-assign them. This is the richest school-finance table in either report: School Lunch $429,570.62 receipts / $437,642.03 disbursements; Title I #305 opening MINUS $48,260.80; PL 94-142 #240 $319,675.00 receipts closing MINUS $15,062.97; '50/50 Grant Sped Tuitions' opening MINUS $136,411.97, $614,230.00 receipts, closing MINUS $112,882.47; Chapter 658 School Athletics $142,482.50 receipts / $108,146.77 disbursements; After School Activities $204,577.58; Extended Day Revolving Fund $243,501.76; School Choice $220,058.00; Non-Resident Tuition $141,031.13; Custodian Special Details $12,401.31. Several funds run persistent NEGATIVE balances. Enterprise funds: Sewer Enterprise $755,298.30 receipts / $611,450.23 disbursements / $742,236.86 closing; Solid Waste/Recycling $269,183.15 / $255,011.63; Water Enterprise $26,487.46 / $19,324.41; Sewer Betterment Fund $708,564.80 / $773,045.00. The 1996/1997/1998 Community Policing grants are still open here at $6.55, $1.97 and $0.66 - a year later than in the FY2013 report, unchanged.

rows.name: Capital project funds by town meeting article
rows.what_it_is: Every open capital article back to 2002, with its project account number, article and meeting, purpose, amount appropriated or forwarded, amount expended/encumbered/transferred, and remaining balance.
rows.grain: one capital item within one article
rows.columns: ART #/YR | PURPOSE | APPROPRIATED FORWARD | EXPENDED/ENCUMBERED/TRANSFERRED | BALANCE
rows.layout: article reference and purpose at left, three money columns; multi-item articles print a header line for the article and then one line per item
rows.printed_total: Grand Total $74,313,023.41 / $12,873,476.33 / $61,439,547.08. Key: 'fwd - forward from FY 13', 'ATM - Annual Town Meeting', 'STM - Special Town Meeting'
rows.notes: THE BIG ONE: article '3084 1 1/14 STM Construct Middle School/High School $72,975,321.00' with $11,874,434.00 spent and $61,100,887.00 remaining - the new middle/high school, voted at the January 2014 Special Town Meeting, dominates the whole schedule. Also '3082 11 5/12 ATM Feasibility Study - Middle School/High School $461,504.82 fwd'. The oldest open article is '3006 08/02 ATM Development of Cemeteries $1,019.01 fwd' - a 2002 article still carrying a balance twelve years later. This is the direct successor to page 76 of the FY2013 report and the item-level detail lines up between the two years.

rows.name: Assessments and revenues by major property class
rows.printed_heading: BOARD OF ASSESSORS / Fiscal 2014 Assessments and Revenues by Major Property Class
rows.what_it_is: FY2014 valuation, share of the levy, tax rate and tax levy for each of the five DOR major property classes.
rows.columns: Property Class | Levy Percent | Valuation by Class | Tax Rate | Tax Levy
rows.layout: five columns, one row per class plus a TOTALS row
rows.notes: Residential 89.9122% / 1,013,879,421 / 18,239,690.78. Open Space is printed as '-0-' - the town classifies nothing as open space. A single tax rate of 17.99 applies to every class, so Lunenburg does NOT split its tax rate. FY2013's report has no equivalent table.

rows.name: Valuation and tax rate history, nine years
rows.what_it_is: Tax rate, total valuation, number of accounts, tax levy and year-over-year percentage change for fiscal years 2006 through 2014.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Tax Rate | Total Valuation | Accounts | Tax Levy | Change (%)
rows.layout: six columns, newest year first
rows.notes: IMPORTANT CROSS-YEAR DISCREPANCY: this table gives FY2013's tax rate as 17.30 and FY2012's as 16.83. The FY2013 report's own version of this history table ends its tax-rate run at 16.83, i.e. it is offset by one year against this one. Do not treat the two years' history tables as interchangeable without checking the alignment. Values here: 2014 17.99 / 1,127,633,052 / 5,092 / 20,286,118.60 / 3.6765; 2013 17.30 / 1,131,029,744 / 5,054 / 19,566,814.57; 2012 16.83 / 1,120,966,561 / 5,351 / 18,865,867.23; 2011 16.16 / 1,114,282,889 / 5,185; 2010 14.20 / 1,227,274,404 / 5,028; 2009 13.04; 2008 12.23; 2007 12.13; 2006 12.41.

rows.name: Abstract of assessments by property class code
rows.what_it_is: FY2014 accounts, total valuation and average value for each DOR property class code.
rows.columns: Property Class Code/Description | Accts | Class Valuation | Avg.Value
rows.layout: four columns plus a TOTALS row
rows.notes: Adds a class that FY2013's version does not name the same way: '012 - 043 Mixed Use Properties 39 / 24,329,248 / 623,826'. Residential Single Family 3,443 accounts / 844,812,100 / 245,370 average. Apartments: only 7 accounts averaging 1,272,000. The TOTALS row prints no average, correctly.

rows.name: Exemptions, abatements and overlay, five years
rows.printed_heading: Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements
rows.what_it_is: The overlay account for FY2010-FY2014: overlay raised, overlay deficits, charges against it, potential liability and amount released.
rows.grain: one overlay component (rows) by fiscal year (columns)
rows.columns: Description | FY2014 | FY2013 | FY2012 | FY2011 | FY2010
rows.layout: component down the left, five year columns - the TRANSPOSE of how FY2013 printed the same data
rows.notes: Assessor's Overlay 145,256.60 / 156,740.57 / 141,918.23 / 124,378.48 / 141,582.64 - the FY2013-FY2010 values match the FY2013 report exactly, so the two years' figures are consistent here even though the layout is transposed. The row heading 'Charges to 6/30/2010' is reprinted verbatim in the FY2014 report even though it now carries FY2014 figures - a stale label carried across at least two years.

rows.name: New growth revenue by fiscal year
rows.what_it_is: Added valuation from new growth, the tax rate applied to it, the resulting new revenue and the percentage change, for FY2007 through FY2014.
rows.columns: Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change (%)
rows.layout: five columns, newest first
rows.notes: This table has a Tax Rate column that FY2013's version does not, and the tax rates in it are the SHIFTED series (2014 uses 17.30, 2013 uses 16.83) rather than the levy-year series in the Valuation and Tax History table on the same page - the two tables on one page do not use the same rate for the same year. Also the FY2012 figure differs from the FY2013 report: here FY2012 added valuation is 27,729,619 / 448,111 new revenue / +137.43%, whereas the FY2013 report's series has no such row. Values: 2014 17,200,564 / 297,571 / -7.55; 2013 19,124,255 / 321,862 / -28.17.

rows.name: Treasurer's cash by bank account
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / Treasurer's Cash as of 6/30/14
rows.what_it_is: Every bank account the Treasurer held at 30 June 2014 with its balance.
rows.layout: single label/amount column
rows.printed_total: Total Cash per Treasurer 6/30/14 $8,861,659.32
rows.notes: Compare to FY2013's $8,322,294.68. The bank list has changed between years: FY2014 adds Citizens Bank, Enterprise Bank, North Middlesex Savings, Unibank (two accounts), Webster Bank, Touchstone Library Trust Funds, MMDT Highway Bond Issue, MMDT Playground Fund, MMDT Arts Lottery, Fidelity Bank ARRA EECBG, Fidelity Bank Sewer Hook-Up, Fidelity Bank EOCD Grant, Fidelity Bank Senior Grant; FY2013's 'Old Mutual Trust Funds' and 'TD BankNorth Stabilization' are renamed 'Touchstone Library Trust Funds' and 'TD BankNorth Zoning Stabilization'. FY2014's version does NOT leak the preparer's filesystem path, which FY2013's did.

rows.name: Trust funds summary report
rows.printed_heading: TRUST FUNDS FISCAL YEAR 2014 SUMMARY REPORT
rows.what_it_is: Every town trust fund, by account number and NAME, with beginning principal and earnings balances, contributions to principal, net earnings, disbursements from principal, transfers of earnings, ending cash value, unrealized gain/loss and ending market value. Grouped into CEMETERY FUNDS, CONSERVATION FUNDS, LIBRARY FUNDS, SCHOLARSHIP FUNDS, MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS and STABILIZATION FUNDS, each with a SUBTOTALS row, plus a separate block for funds held at other banks.
rows.columns: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | BEGINNING EARNINGS | CONTRIBUTE TO PRINCIPAL | NET EARNINGS | DISBURSE FROM PRINCIPAL | TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS | ENDING CASH VALUE | UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | ENDING MARKET VALUE
rows.layout: eleven columns; every row is complete on one line
rows.notes: THIS SOLVES THE FY2013 PROBLEM. FY2013's trust fund table has clean rows of money with NO fund names in the text layer at all; FY2014's has account numbers AND names, and many of the FY2014 opening balances equal the FY2013 closing balances - so the FY2014 table can be used to LABEL the FY2013 rows. Named funds include PERPETUAL CARE BEQUEST, C. ALLEN HEADSTONE, SALE OF CEMETERY LOTS, CONSERVATION LAND PURCHASE, R. BURTON / H. BENJAMIN / G. HUBBARD / I. KIMBALL CONSERVATION, thirteen named library book bequests (CHARLES DICKERSON, CATHERINE WATSON, FRANCIS CALDWELL, SUSAN DICKINSON, EMMA DIMOND, AUGUST TAYLOR, STEPHEN STICKNEY, LIZZIE TAYLOR, EBENEZER BAILEY, LUCY GOODRICH, SUSAN HOWARD, ADIN & MAY ESTABROOK, IRVIN & HAZEL KIMBALL), ANNIE & ARTHUR BILLINGS CULTURAL TRUST, DORA HAVEN COWDRY SCHOLARSHIP ($369,654.10 - the largest single trust), BETH N CURTIS MEMORIAL SCHOLAR, BARBARA NELSON SCHOLARSHIP, PHILIP CROUSE, AMERICAN LEGION POOR, J & M HOWARD SDWLK/GRDS, WORTHY POOR INCOME, GAZEBO RESTORATION, LUNENBURG POST #283 (new in FY2014 at $6,941.18), STABILIZATION ($1,299,077.98 after a $286,958.00 contribution), ARTS LOTTERY (MMDT), PLAYGROUND TRUST (MMDT), MABEL ALLEN STOCK #20376, JOSEPH HARWOOD STOCK, OLD MUTUAL PBHG FUNDS, ZONING INCENTIVE STABILIZATION (TD BANKNORTH). One MISCELLANEOUS FUNDS subtotal line is printed as '.' rather than 'SUBTOTALS'.

rows.name: Five years outstanding debt, and authorized unissued debt
rows.printed_heading: FIVE YEARS OUTSTANDING DEBT / As of June 30, 2014
rows.what_it_is: Long-term debt outstanding by purpose for each of FY2010-FY2014, split between within and outside the general debt limit; plus a list of debt authorized but not yet issued.
rows.grain: one debt purpose (rows) by year (columns); one authorized purpose in the second block
rows.layout: purpose at left, five year columns; second block is Amount / Purpose
rows.printed_total: Total Long-Term Indebtedness 22,140,230 / 24,298,666 / 26,479,504 / 27,097,992 / 29,122,015. Authorized unissued total 77,129,843
rows.notes: The five-year run ties exactly to FY2013's version of the same table for the four overlapping years. THE STRIKING NUMBER: authorized unissued debt jumps to $77,129,843 because of a new line '72,975,321 School Construction' - against FY2013's authorized unissued total of about $2.4M. Also new since FY2013: '411,000 School Feasibility Study Bond', '425,000 Fire Equipement' [sic], '624,000 Land Acquisition', '2,200,000 Sewer Construction'. Same footnote as FY2013: '(1)Principal amount only. Excludes lease and installment purchase obligations, overlapping debt and unfunded pension liability.'

rows.name: Debt repayment schedule to maturity
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2014
rows.what_it_is: Year-by-year principal, interest and total due on every outstanding debt issue, named issue by issue, from FY2015 out to FY2047, with a TOTAL column.
rows.grain: one debt issue (three rows each: PRINCIPAL, INTEREST, TOTAL)
rows.layout: a wide landscape grid split across three pages: page 40 = FY2015-2028, page 41 = FY2029-2045, page 42 = 2046-2047 plus the TOTAL column
rows.printed_total: GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL $22,140,229; GRAND TOTAL INTEREST $6,338,637; TOTAL DEBT $28,478,866
rows.notes: VASTLY better than FY2013's version, which lost its issue-name column entirely. Here every issue is named: MASS WATER POOL 3*, 4*, 5*, 7*, 9*, 13*, 14*, MUNICIPAL PURPOSE, MUNICIPAL PURPOSE SEWER, MUNICIPAL PURPOSE WATER. Extraction caveat on page 42: the label column and the value column have slipped by one row, so the TOTAL figures print one line ABOVE the label they belong to (e.g. 'INTEREST $31,011 / TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST $3,332 / MASS WATER POOL 4* $34,343' - the $34,343 is MASS WATER POOL 3's total, not 4's). 'MASS WATER POLL TRUST' is a recurring typo for POOL. The grand total principal $22,140,229 ties to the balance sheet's long-term debt $22,140,230 within a dollar.

rows.name: Collection of taxes
rows.printed_heading: TOWN OF LUNENBURG / COLLECTION OF TAXES / FY-2014
rows.what_it_is: For every tax, excise, betterment and user-charge commitment outstanding - by levy year - the balance brought forward, new commitments, adjustments, refunds, payments, abatements, transfers, and the balance remaining.
rows.grain: one tax type and levy year
rows.columns: FISCAL YEAR | FORWARD | COMMITTMENTS | ADJUSTMENTS | REFUNDS | PAYMENTS | ABATEMENTS | TRANSFERS | BALANCES
rows.layout: eight money columns, one row per commitment; page 43 covers MVE / PP / RE by levy year, page 44 covers liens, betterments and user charges
rows.notes: FY2013's version of this table (page 83) is unreadable - the row labels are entirely absent. Here every row is labelled ('1997 MVE', '2014 RE', 'SEWER BETT COMM', 'MEADOW BETTERMENT', 'SLIEN PRIN COM TO RE'). Extraction caveat: money columns are separated by variable whitespace and blank cells collapse, so column position must come from the x-coordinate, not from token order. Notable: motor vehicle excise is still being chased back to 1997, and personal property back to 1998, with balances of a few thousand dollars each. 2014 RE commitments 19,747,418.40 with payments (19,193,857.66). SEWER BETTERMENT carries 5,265,358.33 forward and 4,871,360.01 remaining. Several rows in the FY2013 report's mangled version can be matched to these labelled rows by their forward balances.

rows.name: Burials in town cemeteries, by month
rows.what_it_is: Every person buried in a Lunenburg cemetery during 2014, month by month, with age, which cemetery, a cremation marker, and for veterans the conflict they served in.
rows.layout: two side-by-side blocks (Jan-Jul left, Aug-Dec right) with month sub-headings; column headings printed once across the top
rows.notes: Cemetery is a one-letter code, N or S (North / South), which is readable here - in FY2013's OCR version the same column is unreadable noise. Veteran service is written into the name field: 'Wallace l. Douglas WWII', 'Ronald W. Bishop Viet Nam', 'Bernard P. Keaveny Korea', 'Robert D. Gonynor WWII', 'Warren E. Ward WWII', 'Henry V. Buiwit WWII'. '*Denotes Cremation' - and the majority of 2014 burials carry the asterisk. JANUARY and FEBRUARY have no entries at all. Also on this page: the cemetery mapping system URL http://www.map.ramaker.com/ecims/.

rows.name: Council on Aging services and participation
rows.what_it_is: The COA's staff and board membership, its service volume, and a two-column grid of the ongoing programs it runs.
rows.grain: one program (grid) / one staff or board member (list)
rows.layout: a two-column grid of program names under 'The chart below shows some of the ongoing services that we provide:', plus staff and board name lists
rows.notes: Carries usable operating figures inside the prose: 'In FY 14 the Council on Aging provided 10,453 units of service to 732 participants', '62% of them women, and 38% of them men'; '$121,695 from the municipal budget for salaries and expenses'; MART funds the van drivers' salaries and half the dispatcher; 'Eagle House volunteers clocked 3000 hours of service'; '11 people participate in the Senior Tax Work Off program and they provided over 900 hours of labor'. The staffing is given in hours per week rather than FTE. Note the funding sentence is a direct example of a budget line NOT being the cost of the service - MART and the Department of Elder Affairs pay for staff that never appear in the $121,695.

rows.name: Town-owned buildings and properties maintained by DPW
rows.what_it_is: The list of buildings and properties the DPW facilities division maintains.

Q3 casino repeal, Q4 earned sick time (YES 2054, NO 2110 - Lunenburg narrowly voted NO on a measure that passed statewide). QUESTION 5 IS THE INTERESTING ONE: a non-binding instruction to the state representative on a constitutional amendment about corporate personhood, and it appears ONLY in Precinct B (585-221) because Precinct B is the only Lunenburg precinct in the 3rd Worcester District - so the question was on one precinct's ballot and not the other three's. Full official question text is reproduced, which is several hundred words per question.

rows.name: Town and school employee compensation, calendar 2014
rows.what_it_is: Every person paid by the Town of Lunenburg or the school district in calendar year 2014, alphabetically by surname, with gross wages and the paying department.
rows.columns: LAST NAME | FIRST NAME | WAGES | DEPARTMENT
rows.layout: TWO name/wage/department column groups side by side per line - so each printed line holds two different employees
rows.notes: Directly extractable, unlike FY2013's version where the surname, given name, department and amount runs were emitted as four separate long lines and could not be re-paired. The trap here is that each text line holds TWO complete records side by side ('ADAMOWICZ JOSEPH 23,924.63 SCHOOL BERTHIAUME RONALD 5,819.89 SCHOOL') and the alphabetical sequence runs down the left column first, so a naive line-by-line read produces an interleaved order. Departments seen: SCHOOL, POLICE, FIRE, DPW, LIBRARY, COA, SELECTMEN, PLANNING, TOWN CLERK, CEMETERY, TREASURER, VET SERV. Note the heading says CALENDAR 2014, i.e. calendar-year wages, NOT the fiscal year that the rest of the accountant's tables use - the two cannot be added together or compared line for line. FY2013's equivalent is headed 'Payroll Report' with no period stated at all.
